name: HDFC Life Insurance Company Ltd
title: HDFC Life Insurance Company Ltd - 540777 - Transcript Of Earnings Conference Call - H1 FY'27

read.thesis: Life insurer grows ahead of industry with VNB +12% and NBM 24.7%, but persistency softening in unit-linked and proposed commission cuts cloud the bancassurance channel; no supply-side capacity signal.

triggers.label: Unit-linked renewal persistency softening
triggers.quote: Persistency was softer on renewal collections in our unit -linked book amidst market volatility

triggers.label: Distribution commission cuts proposed
triggers.quote: IRDAI has released consultation papers on the economics of insurance distribution, which propose significant changes for the industry.

triggers.label: Individual APE +9% H1, Q2 APE +13%
triggers.quote: This took our H1 individual APE growth to 9%. Overall APE grew faster, at 13% in Q2 and 11% in H1.

guidance.value: VNB growth in line with APE or slightly ahead
guidance.quote: we will continue with the objective of delivering VNB growth in line with APE or slightly ahead of it

guidance.value: Grow in line with industry in FY27
guidance.quote: We expect to sustain this momentum and grow in line with the industry in FY27.
15% is something that we will achieve just mathematically.

red_flags.label: Contingent liability rising; Palghar GST penalty figure ambiguity
red_flags.quote: the contingent liabilities also increased slightly to INR2,207 crores as of September versus INR1,870 crores as of March

evasions.topic: Variable annuity margin vs traditional annuities
evasions.quote: We are not really getting into specifics of that. It's a profitable product, that's all I can say.
Whatever you see in our balance sheet today will be the right number.

summary.headline: HDFC Life H1 FY27 VNB rose 12% to ₹2,037 crore at a 24.7% margin, while solvency fell to 180% on capital consumption.
summary.overview: Q2 individual APE growth of 13% (overall) and 11% in H1 kept HDFC Life ahead of the private industry, with individual weighted received premium up 11% in Q2 and market share up 10bps to 16.2%. VNB reached ₹2,037 crore (up 12%, Q2 up 15%) and margin expanded to 24.7% from 24.5%. Persistency softened on unit-linked renewals and a non-par cohort, and the EV walk showed negative operating and investment variances from equity underperformance, yield rises and wider credit spreads. Solvency fell to 180%, prompting a ₹500 crore subordinated debt raise. Management spent much of the call on the IRDAI distribution-economics consultation paper, where it was non-committal on specifics.

financial_highlights.change: Regulatory requirement 150%; ₹500 crore sub-debt expected to add about 4 percentage points
Q2 individual weighted received premium +11% vs private industry +10%

segments.name: Bancassurance (HDFC Bank)
segments.commentary: HDFC Bank-sourced individual APE grew 12% in Q2, slightly ahead of company growth; the bank accounts for about 48% of APE in Q2 but less than 40% of NBP. Other bancassurance partners grew 13% in Q2, and a new J&K Bank partnership was announced.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Agency grew 13% in H1, faster than the company and the agency market. Branches opened in the last ~30 months contribute about 17% of agency business versus 12% a year ago; protection and annuity together are about 30% of channel mix versus 15% previously.

segments.name: Product mix (individual APE, H1)
segments.commentary: Unit-linked 45%, non-par savings 22% (from about 18%), participating 13%, annuity 12% (versus 4-5% previously), retail protection 8% (from about 7%). Retail protection grew 33% in H1; protection plus riders is 11% of APE; credit protect grew 19%.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Pension business AUM reached ₹1.8 lakh crore, up 28% YoY. MSCI ESG rating upgraded to AAA from AA.

guidance_outlook: Expects individual APE growth in FY27 to be in line with the industry, after 9% in H1.
VNB growth to be in line with APE or slightly ahead; management will prioritise VNB growth over margin, with margin an outcome of mix and competition.
GST cost benefit (about 15% cost reduction) gets fully baked into the business model from H2 FY27; scale recovery is expected to lift margins, but most will be reinvested.
Expects persistency to recover by year-end, particularly unit-linked renewals, with the non-par cohort run-off progressing.
Expects to remain comfortably above the 150% regulatory minimum through FY27 after the ₹500 crore sub-debt, which is expected to close in the current quarter.
Protection growth expected to normalise in H2 against a 57% base (H2 FY26 post-GST), while remaining strong on a two-year CAGR basis.
On the expense ratio (about 21%, over half commissions), management said reaching 15% under the discussion-paper commissions is mathematically achievable; glide path still to be determined.
Management views 1 January as an unlikely effective date for distribution reforms; the earliest plausible date is 1 April.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: over 250 agency branches added in the last ~30 months; branches contribute about 17% of agency business.
Technology architecture rollout is expected to support customer- and partner-facing capabilities; investments to continue.
Capital: solvency at 180% after capital consumption from writing long-term profitable products; management expects RBC transition discussions and a timeline around next year.
demand_pricing: Unit-linked demand resilient despite equity volatility; renewal collections softer in unit-linked, while new business flows into unit-linked remained strong.
HDFC Bank IRRs made competitive via higher yields, enabling a share recovery in non-par; no change in commercial payouts, according to management.
Annuity mix rose on variable annuity launch (Q4 FY26); new business premium share of annuity is about 17% (from about 14%).
Average ticket size: savings about ₹1.1 lakh, protection about ₹40-45 thousand; protection at 8% of APE implies about 2.5x that share on policy count.

Sector competition: management says the market is intensely competitive; the proposed commission caps are expected to hit brokers and corporate agents most, then banks, with agency least affected (management's categorisation).

qa_highlights.question: What changed at HDFC Bank that drove growth recovery, and did IRRs or commissions change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited granular branch-level engagement, a withdrawal of extra contests about a year ago, and fixing credit and people issues over the last 3-4 months. Rates were kept competitive with higher yields; no change in commercial payouts.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EV walk operating variance is persistency, and what drove the investment variance?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating variance was primarily unit-linked persistency plus residual non-par run-off. Investment variance came from equity returns of about 3-3.5% versus 5% expected, a 25-30bps short-end yield rise, and wider credit spreads.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the capital consumption and how will solvency evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term profitable products lock capital under the current regime; the sub-debt adds about 4 percentage points, and management expects to remain comfortably above 150% through FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How do the proposed commission limits affect VNB margin and EoM?
qa_highlights.answer: Expense ratio about 21%, with commissions more than half; under the proposed levels, commissions fall to half or less, so a 15% EoM is mathematically achievable, subject to scale and glide-path considerations.

qa_highlights.question: Is persistency pressure concentrated in TULIPs or the wider unit-linked book?
qa_highlights.answer: Not limited to any product: pressure is uniform across unit-linked. Recent unit-linked persistency variance is captured in the EV; management expects most to be recovered by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit life share, and what is the HDFC Bank share of it?
qa_highlights.answer: HDFC Bank contributes less than one-third of credit life business, which is diversified across MFIs, NBFCs, banks and the HDFC Group. Management would not disclose the bundled-versus-separate premium collection mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Palghar GST demand, and does the appeal change the provisioning stance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the balance-sheet figure is correct and it is treated as a contingent liability (₹942 crore base, with the accrued total in the books). Interest is excluded and management is confident on the merits, so no provision was taken; contingent liabilities rose to ₹2,207 crore from ₹1,870 crore.

risks_watch: Distribution-reform consultation: commission caps, closed-architecture tilt and possible credit-life restrictions could affect bancassurance and group business; draft regulation timing is uncertain.
Unit-linked renewal persistency and the non-par cohort run-off: recovery is expected by year-end and needs monitoring.
Solvency at 180% with capital consumption ongoing; RBC transition timing (possibly next year) is open.
Palghar GST demand (₹942 crore base, contingent liability) and the reported ₹2,423 crore figure in the appeal: the exact amount and solvency impact remained unclear.
Protection growth normalisation in H2 as the GST-exemption base effect kicks in (base growth of 57% in H2 FY26).
Equity and yield volatility driving investment variance and the EV walk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and VNB momentum, and on the bank channel recovery, but evasive on distribution reforms, the VNB margin path, variable annuity economics and the Palghar figure, which management deferred until drafts are issued.
key_quotes: We remain confident in the long-term opportunity for the industry and in our ability to further strengthen our position within it.
Our approach is fairly clear and we'll stay with that, that we'll want to maximize VNB growth, and margins will be an outcome of everything that we see around us.
No, the regulator and government have been very reasonable in their expectation when the GST change happened because it was very, very clear and visible to the customer.

adds.what: over 250 agency branches added in the last ~30 months (branches contribute ~17% of agency business)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 individual APE growth in line with the industry (after 9% in H1) and VNB growth in line with or slightly ahead of APE, backed by agency branch build-out, protection/annuity momentum and a J&K Bank partnership, but no quantified capacity or order numbers were given for the FY27 guidance.
